## samb-p01-v01 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)

**Question.** Under what auspice does the inquiry into relation open?

**Premises.**
- With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference (bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasaha).
- By whom all things are proved (sarvārthasādhitā); world-traffic (lokayātrā) is whose work (kṛtiḥ).
- Him, Śiva, by own will (svecchayā), we praise (stumaḥ).

**Inference.** Auspice: the Lord whose will works world-traffic proves all things with difference-and-non-difference-relation.


### Open
- Feminine adjectives (saha, sādhitā) lack an overt noun — implied śakti, or absolute construction; held open.
- svecchayā's agency (his will grounding relation vs our will in praising) held open; read as his (svātantrya seed).

C1 commentary · 173 words
## samb-p01-v01 — C1 **SUMMARY.** Relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference proves all things; world-traffic is his work — Śiva, by own will, praised. His body dawns made of relation: conquering though one, world-self, light, supreme Lord. Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert — impossible; won selfhood or not, metaphor, not definition. Teaching self-obtaining to non-beings drops two-seatedness: form-fusion alone stands as relation's sense. No unbroken nearness — it misses relation; else iron bars. So the many's form-fusion: one-selfhood alone. Others say the many need no barring in oneness: things unmixed, thought joins them. No mere thought, this — past warding, like snake-error clinging to a shining. Clinging is no thing-like-shining but trailing after it: error, that shining strayed. So many-seen-as-one finds warrant — statable, told clear in recognition's path. *Rasa: vīra (triumph) of demolition and retorsion — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: three refusals, then the opponent's verse testifying against itself. The vyabhicāri is wonder that joining was never mere thought. Śāstric triumph-relish: truth winning by the adversary's own words.*

## samb-p01-v03 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Are awaiting or dependence the relation of inert things?

**Premises.**
- Awaiting (apekṣā) and dependence (pāratantryam) are no relation (na saṃbandhaḥ) for the two inert (jaḍātmanoḥ).
- From impossibility (asaṃbhavāt): even where selfhood is won (ātmalābhe'pi), it is metaphor (upacāraḥ), not definition (lakṣaṇā).
- Prose (p.2-3): the sprout 'awaits' the seed only by courtesy; awaiting, longing-for-the-other's-disposal, checking one's own will are will-determinations (saṃkalpaviśeṣa) — and will is consciousness's.

**Inference.** First reduction fails: awaiting-language smuggles in the conscious relatum it should supply.

## samb-p01-v05 — argument map

**Speaker.** Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

**Question.** Is uninterruptedness the relation — and what positively is it?

**Premises.**
- Not uninterruptedness (na ānantaryam): it misses relation (asaṃbandhāt) — else it would hold of iron bars (ayaḥśalākayoḥ).
- Prose (p.2): distant father-son lack it, adjacent iron bars (even pervading substances) have it — neither necessary nor sufficient.
- Hence (tena): fusion (śleṣaḥ) of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood (aikātmyam eva).

**Inference.** Third reduction fails (with the iron-bars counterexample); positive thesis: relation is the many's form-fused one-selfhood.

## samb-p01-v06 — argument map

**Speaker.** Opponent (Dharmakīrtian; SP 5cd per MacCracken/Jha)

**Question.** Do the many need any unity at all?

**Premises.**
- No barring (bādhaḥ) of the many even in one's unity (ekasyaikye'pi) — they say, as others do.
- Things unmixed in themselves (amiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāḥ) — thought (kalpanā) joins them (yojayati).
- Witness: Dharmakīrti's Sambandhaparīkṣā v.5cd (Jha Philosophy of Relations; MacCracken) — the opponent's proof-text, quoted against him.

**Inference.** The Buddhist position in its own voice: unmixed things, thought-joined; unity needs no seat.

**Question.** What makes error stick?

**Premises.**

- It is following-after-shining (ābhāsānusāritvaṃ): error is just that — an erred shining (bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat).
- Prose (p.5): all errors concern resembling — but beyond resembling, errors hold by shining-clinging; else the silver-shell could not guide. Transaction-guiding seeming must follow the shining.

**Inference.** Error sticks by following shining, not resembling things: seeming that guides must trail being.

C1 commentary · 172 words
## samb-p02-v10 — C1 **SUMMARY.** Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — the consciousness-bodied need no forcing. The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference inside non-difference's shine. One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply. The many still reach oneness through one-word superimposition — pot-cloth says it. A second relation stands, qualifier with qualified, for helping's sake: it serves to know. Even in many, twoness holds — double-grasp-begot, like the king's horses, chariots, men. Grasp 'of king' stands one, toward its own kind; 'man' the other, sharing the master-kind's bond. 'The king's man' — thought after, in relation's field, by this; or the first two thought — all three, always. Spoken by the sixth, relation settles in the qualifier — reaching oneness with the qualified, yet keeping its own shape. *Rasa: vīra (triumph) of fitted joinery — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: each fitting holds — twoness in manyness, oneness in twoness, shape kept in settling. The vyabhicāri is grammarian wonder that counting thinks. Joinery relished.*

C1 commentary · 110 words
## samb-p03-v19 — C1 **SUMMARY.** One short of the pure chief, secondaries mutually fit — the king's man, and the brahmin's. By other chiefs, other unities — relation-called of secondaries: the king's horse, man. Thus relation's course is told: intellects resting on Māyā-knowers, of varied views, driving transaction. Not deluded, though called so — all, moment by moment, grounded in endless-awareness reflection called self-awareness. Told, self-awareness-proved, unrefuted, useful — relation in recognition: full apparatus besides. *Rasa: vīra (triumph) of sealing — The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the proof closes the way treatises close — measured, told, defended, sealed. The vyabhicāri is relief that delusion is denied without new machinery. Seal relished.*
